mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the permission matrix fact leaves the Allowed relation unconstrained. The LeastPrivilege and PermissionCompleteness assertions require specific role-operation pairs to be allowed or denied; without the fact, Alloy can construct models where the matrix is inconsistent or incomplete.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermMatrixViolation { some r: Role, op: OperationKind | not (r -> op in PermMatrix.Allowed) and (r = Member and op = PostTasks) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the append-only constraint allows two audit entries with the same id to have different fields. The AppendOnly assertion checks that identical audit IDs imply identical content; without the fact, Alloy can find models where an audit entry is mutated.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.id = ae2.id and ae1.task_id != ae2.task_id }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the one-audit-per-task constraint allows tasks without audit entries. The AuditCompleteness assertion requires every task to have exactly one audit entry; without the fact, Alloy can construct models where a task exists with no audit trail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some t: Task | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.task_id = t }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the cross-team isolation fact allows team members to be associated with tasks from other teams. The NoInformationLeakage assertion checks that team-membership boundaries are respected; without the fact, Alloy can find models where a member of Team1 can see a task from Team2.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamLeakage { some t1, t2: Task, tm: TeamMembership | tm.team = t1.team_id and t1.team_id != t2.team_id and tm.team = t2.team_id }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the one-owner constraint allows tasks to have zero, one, or many owners. The OwnershipExclusivity assertion checks that every task has exactly one owner; without the fact, Alloy can construct models where a task has no owner or multiple owners, violating the ownership-based access control invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some t: Task | no u: User | u = t.owner_id }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the owner-must-be-member constraint allows a task owner to not belong to the task's team. The OwnershipBasedAccess assertion requires that the owner is a member of the task's team (enabling edit/delete permissions); without the fact, Alloy can find models where an owner has no team membership, breaking the access-control model.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnerNotInTeam { some t: Task | no tm: TeamMembership | tm.user = t.owner_id and tm.team = t.team_id }
